utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We are now in public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And just one other matter, Your Honour. The psychiatrist is requesting the ability to sit and observe the accused during this testimony. Mr. Domazet has no objection. She is just standing outside. If security could just escort her to the room, I would appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. And I should tell you that I ran into Mr. Rohde in the corridors after you raised this issue of getting the accused back to the Detention Unit as soon as possible, and he said he would do everything he could to make that happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The Prosecution appreciates that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Right. Now, who do we have? The investigator, do we?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecution calls investigator Garry Selsky.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm sorry, Mr. Domazet. You're still standing up.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm waiting your permission that Mr. Tanaskovic can come here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It's not a question of our permission. He's entitled to come in. Whatever arrangement you've entered into in relation to him is a matter between counsel, not the Court. But thank you for asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, sir, would you please make the solemn declaration in the card which the usher is showing you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sit down, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I promised Mr. Tanaskovic that I would inform him as soon as the previous witness is finished with the testimony. Since I can't go and inform him personally, could the usher go and inform him? Mr. Tanaskovic could not join us before this because we were in closed session. So he is now waiting in the Defence counsel's room, and I wouldn't want him to miss the testimony of this new witness. I don't think there is any need for that. I think that we avoided any potential problems by not having him present during the testimony of previous witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: He will have to be escorted here, so the usher is obviously the appropriate person. Thanks, Tomas. Yes, Mr. Ossogo.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Selsky. Will you please introduce to the Chamber -- will you tell us your name, please.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: My name is Garry Paul Selsky.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Could you tell the Chamber about your professional experience in a few words? What kind of professional background do you have?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I'm from Canada. I spent from 1972 to 1998 in the Royal Canadian Mounted Police as an investigator, investigating serious crimes. I worked in immigration, drugs, internal affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: And you joined the Office of the Prosecutor when?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: In September of 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Did you take part in the investigation in the case of the accused, Mitar Vasiljevic [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Not specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Were you responsible for the preparation of the case against Dragan Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I am so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. There is a problem with the translation there. Was your question: Was he taking part in the investigation of Nikolic, another accused, not Mr. Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, Mr. President, but there is a delay with the translation, and I am waiting for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We're hopefully very conscious of the delay that is necessary, but you were mistranslated. It's been recorded as having asked the witness whether he took part in the investigation of the accused Mitar Vasiljevic, and his answer is, "Not specifically." Now, may I suggest you ask the question again, and this time hopefully it will be translated as referring to Nikolic, not Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. So I will repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Did you take part in the investigation concerning Mr. Dragan Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes, since his arrest April 22nd, the year 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Can you tell us: Who is Mr. Dragan Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Mr. Dragan Nikolic is an indicted person by the Tribunal, the first indictment to take place. He is charged as a commander of Susica camp, in the municipality of Vlasenica, and he has many counts against his activities, his alleged activities, between April of 1992 to September of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Can you give us the date of his arrest, please?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: He was arrested on the 22nd of April, 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Can you tell us which representative of the Tribunal was present at his arrest?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Ossogo, I think, if I may just issue a word of caution here. The circumstances of Mr. Nikolic's arrest are very much in issue in a motion which he has brought seeking to be released as a result of the circumstances of his arrest. Now, if you need to go into them, by all means do so but I suggest you do so with some care.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. This is a case involving quite specific details, so let me get to the next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: When Mr. Nikolic was arrested, Mr. Selsky, did you find on Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Mr. Nikolic's person identity cards?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: No. I wasn't present when his effects, his wallet, was taken from him, but his wallet was turned over to me at the Tribunal on the 25th of April, 2000, by Bob Reid, acting chief of investigations.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: And the wallet that you were given by Mr. Bob Reid, did you have an opportunity to see whether there were any identity cards there that were confiscated at the time of Mr. Nikolic's arrest?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes. I went through the wallet and looked at the contents, and seized them or put them into plastic bags, each piece of -- item that I found.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Were there any identity cards there that could serve as evidence of Mr. Nikolic's identity?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes. There was three pieces of identification in the names of Vidovic and Petric. Both are -- some of the identification had photographic pictures identifying or showing the picture of Dragan Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have here photocopies of those identity cards with photographs on them depicting Mr. Nikolic. We will distribute them to the usher so that he could give it to the witness and the witness could proceed with identifying them.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Is this a copy of identity cards that were confiscated and turned over to you?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Is that what you have before you?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: This appears to be a copy of the identification that I examined and processed and put the originals in a clear plastic bag.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have now here the three plastic bags containing identity cards of Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Let's wait and see if there's some challenge to it. You tender these documents that were found on Mr. Nikolic. Is there any objection to them, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. They will be Exhibit P144. Is that right? No. I'm sorry. They --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: They are Exhibits P111.1 and 111.2 and 111.3.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm proposing, just in order to see these identity cards clearly, to distribute these three originals that are in plastic bags.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Do you mind if we just get on with it, Mr. Ossogo? This is a very straightforward issue. Do we need to see them? They are photostats. May I suggest you ask the witness, "Do they bear photographs of Mr. Nikolic?" and then we can him ask what was said to Mr. Nikolic about it. We don't really need to do this unless there is some challenge, and there hasn't been so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Are these the originals that you mentioned previously, Mr. Selsky, that had been put in plastic bags and are in fact identity cards of Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes. These are the identity cards that we retrieved from Mr. Nikolic's wallet and made photocopies as you have before you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will not tender these documents because the purpose of them was simply to get a clear picture of the photocopies.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Mr. Selsky, could you please tell us whether Mr. Nikolic gave any kind of statement to the OTP investigators?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Between the 27th of November and the 23rd of March, I spoke to Mr. Nikolic for nine days and interviewed him throughout those nine days.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: This statement that you mentioned, was it recorded? Was it recorded on a videotape?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes. The interview took place in regards to the -- or in adherence to the policies of the Office of the Prosecutor. Mr. Nikolic was present and represented by his lawyer, Mr. Howard Morrison. He was represented by his own interpreter. The interview was videotaped, and he was warned at the beginning of the interview and subsequently at each break. He cooperated through the interview and understood the English-to-Serbian translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Have you asked him about the identity cards that were found on him?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes. The first day he was asked about the contents of his wallet, and he indicated that this identification was obtained by himself, and it was used for two purposes: one was to carry a pistol, and the other false documents were used to obtain health care.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: So he therefore admitted having those three identity cards on him, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: And he admitted using all those three identity cards, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He had back problems of which he had to get X-rays and different treatments, and it was used for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: You have told us that the video recording was done during the interview. We would ask that the part that was videotaped be shown here so that you can see whether this is indeed the man that you mentioned and whether this was the situation described by you. So I will now ask our technical audio booth to show us this tape. This is Prosecution evidence P114.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Ossogo --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We also have a transcript of this tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: -- is this really necessary? Surely the transcript will do. If there is some challenge to what is said, we can play the tape. We are not trying Mr. Nikolic here. We are trying --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: -- to get in a very simple piece of evidence. And let's get to it. What did he say when he was asked to give an innocent explanation for his possession of these cards? Now, have you got the transcript? Let's get the relevant part of it in.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. President. We thought that perhaps we could show the video and to give then the extra -- the excerpts from the transcript, from pages 26 to 31, and which deal with questions relative to these identity cards. But now could the usher please help me to distribute this transcript? It is 114, Prosecutor's Exhibit 114.1. And we thought we could read as we watched the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is there any objection to this transcript, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. It will be Exhibit 114.1 for the English version.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the interpreters be given some copies, too, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Domazet. Wait a minute. Would you give a copy of the transcript, please, to the interpreters. Yes, Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I have only English version. I don't know if we have a B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Do you have a B/C/S version, Mr. Ossogo?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I'm sorry, but we do not have a version in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, then let's play the tape. You'll get it in one way or the other, I suppose. Let's do it. Play the tape, please. Have the interpreters got copies of the transcript?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right. Let's play the tape, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No translation]

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: "Q. I can assist here, if it helps.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes. They were --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Yes. There's been a trial in Serbia and it should have come up yesterday. Sorry. I've forgetting we have a weekend in between. Friday. You stated you produced identification to the police. Who were the police?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: What -- what type of identification and in what name did you produce it?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: A personal identification card which we have, with a photograph of me, issued in Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: And in whose name was that card?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: It was not in my name.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Okay. I will show you some identification that was taken from you. This is item number 2. It's Republic of Srpska identification in the name of Zoran Petric.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: That's not the photograph that I showed you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Okay. Is that your identification?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: No. I showed a personal ID card. This is different from the refugee pass. I had health problems, and I had to produce this when I was making payments. I had a back injury.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: I will produce an identity card for the army of the Republika Srpska, numbered DO-60/95, in the name of Dobrica Vidovic. Is this what you produced?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: It's not that. This was issued as a permit for carrying a sidearm, a sidearm. I had my own personal pistol, and you -- this permit allowed a person to carry it around through the entire territory of the Republika Srpska. If you went to Banja Luka or Sarajevo or any other place, you would be able to carry an excess and it says that there was a pistol registered.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Okay. For identification purposes, this is item number 3. Item number 4 is the Republika Srpska ID card, number PC-00054220, in the same name of Dobriza Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: This is the ID that I showed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: This one?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: This is what I showed them. And the other two documents were both in the wallet together with the money, the German marks that I had. I don't know if I had any dinars along with that money in the wallet. And also there was an address book in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Why was this in somebody else's name, this identification marked number item 4?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: You mean this identity card?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: This identity card. Why was it in somebody else's versus your name, Dragan Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Because that is the name under which I had registered, and I asked that such a document be issued to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Okay. When did you start using this name, sir?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: 1996. I believe it was in 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: And the other name, Zoran Petric, when did you use that name?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I used it only for the health care purposes. As a refugee, you were entitled to free medical examinations and you paid some symbolic amount for any treatment or medication. For instance, if I had to have an x-ray taken, that would have cost something between 100 pension payments that my mother would get, just the one x-ray of my spine. And refugees had free health care.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Okay. Was this identification used at all to protect your identity, to protect it, keep it secret that you weren't Dragan Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: In a way, yes, even though I stayed with my family and in a small circle of friends who knew me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: So when did you know that there was an indictment against you?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I think that it was immediately after the indictment had been issued. Some people who were listening to the Muslim radio had heard some soldiers who were in the signals corps. They told me how they had heard about it, that an indictment had been issued. And in some areas, one could watch Muslim television; in others, one could not. For instance, in Vlasenica, people in one part of town could catch the programming; the others could not. It was on television once. I did not watch it, but someone told me who had watched it. I don't know -- a relative. I don't know if my brother ever saw it, because I think he was in the part of town that could not watch that programme.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: What year was that? Do you remember? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I believe late 1994, maybe early 1995, but I believe it was later 1994, perhaps around this time of the year. I don't know. Sometime in November.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Okay. Did the authorities assist you with this identification?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I don't know if I can -- I don't know if we can call it authorities. I was assisted by a man who had connections with the authorities, but no, I couldn't say that I was assisted by the authorities, if you look at it as this hierarchical structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: So you didn't go officially to the front door of the refugee identification centre and get the identification? This man helped you with it?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: And you paid this man for helping you?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Do you know who this man is and who he represents?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I know this man, yes, and a friend of his did it. He just said that this would be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Was this man from the police or from the secret service, or from which organisation is he from?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: This was -- he was a member of the reserve civilian police, and the man, I don't know about his friend, the man who actually did it, but as far as the weapons permit is concerned, that was done through another unit. I was not a member of that unit. There was an incident in which I was involved. There were some ethnic Serbs who had attacked me. I had not known them before, and there were four or five of them. And I still have a scar from it, a permanent scar on my head from the blows from the pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: This attack happened why?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: We were sitting in a coffee bar not far from my home. They walked in and they were fairly inebriated. They said that everybody should leave the coffee bar. I was facing away from the entrance. There was a mirror. Some people started leaving. There weren't that many patrons at the time. There were maybe 10 to 15 people inside. They asked me what I was waiting for and they cursed me, and I sort of started rising. I had a pistol on me at the time. Without a reason, they just simply attacked me. Then one of them hit me. I still have a dent here from that blow. And a couple of my teeth were knocked out and so . Then some friends of mine showed up. These people ran away. They just scattered. And then later on they were captured and I think that there was a trial. I haven't been following it. I don't know what the outcome was, but they were charged with attempted murder. And as I said, there was a ban on people carrying weapons. And you had to be a member of a special unit in order to be able to carry your sidearm, and if you wanted to go, let's say, to another municipality just 10 kilometres away, you needed a special permit for that, and this is why I got the permit. And so I got this from someone whom I knew who had a unit. It was a unit of -- a special police unit, and they were able to carry weapons in the entire territory of Republika Srpska. Not heavy weapons, but they could carry sidearms.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Okay. You have identification in Dragan Nikolic and then you have two in different names here as well, Zoran Petric and Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Dobriza Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Yes. Why have two different names with other names as well?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: This ID issued to Zoran Petric, I completely forgot about it. I learned that this man is originally from Banovici and he was killed during the war. I don't know him. And then there was a man from Banovici who lived in Vlasenica as a refugee, and he told me that he could provide me with this document for medical reasons. And as I said, I mean, I mentioned how expensive these things were, medical things, and if they check your identity, if they wanted to verify it, this is why I had this identity card. My mother's pension was about 10 German marks, 10 or 15 a month. And the image that I had developed is something called - I don't know - electromiography --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can stop the tape now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, is that tape P114?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit P114.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to remind that the transcript is numbered as Exhibit 114.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Mr. Selsky, when you look at the transcript in front of you and when you see the transcript of the videotape, does it corresponds to what was taped in your presence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Ossogo, there's no need for that. We've got the tape, and we've got a transcript of it. You don't need to get the witness to verify it. It's either right or it's wrong, but we've got the original in evidence. Now, please will you proceed with any further questions you want to ask him?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was just in case there are any minor differences regarding this but, Mr. President, we're almost finished with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Mr. Selsky, we will now show you a map. This is a map of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and we will ask you to point to some things on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Usher, could you please assist us with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: To save time, Vlasenica appears to be just above the "N" and the "A" in "Herzegovina," and Visegrad we know the position of very well. Is that what you want to get from him, the relationship between two areas?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's exactly so, Your Honour, Visegrad and Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: So please can you just mark with a circle these places on the map?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, do you object to the tender of this as Exhibit 115?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. The map will be Exhibit P115. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should it be marked in red or...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any colour you like, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have now finished with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Selsky, good morning. I would like to ask you a few questions regarding what was shown here today and what we heard from you here today. The transcript from Dragan Nikolic's interview, on page 27, line 9, provides his explanation concerning the ID card. Well, it says here "personal ID card." Is that the exhibit that you have in front of you which is marked as 111.3?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: The first one I showed Mr. Nikolic was item number 2. That shows up as 11.1 [sic].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Does that mean that this is what he had in mind when he said that he needed an ID card because of the health problems he had?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I'm not sure what he had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: This ID card that you mentioned as the second one shown, the one marked as 111.1, can you tell when it was issued? Or if this can be of assistance: Was it done on the 28th of September, 1998? Was it issued on that date?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: When I say "the second one," this is referring to my numbering system I used when discussing with Mr. Nikolic at my interview. So it's not the second one I showed him. It's just -- it's actually the first one I showed him, but it's my number 2, just explaining that. And there is a date on the right-hand lower corner of the identification showing the 28th of 09/98.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And the English translation describes that as the date of issue, Mr. Domazet, if it will save some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So this is the date of issue. So this refugee ID card could be put in use from that date on; isn't that so? So if this ID was used by Mr. Nikolic in order to obtain medical services and he did not show any other refugee ID to you, that means that starting from the end of September 1998, it was possible to use that ID. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: It is a false document, and after that date it could have been used, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, I know it's a false document, but if he used it at all, he could have only used after this day; isn't that so? Was there any mention of the fact that some other ID, personal ID, had to be shown in addition to other documents such as this refugee card?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I don't know exactly which document Mr. Nikolic presented when he -- when he presented these multiple documents to authorities he used.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. But if there was a need to show a personal ID in addition to the refugee card and if he were to show such personal ID card, isn't it a fact that the two ID cards that you have in front of you are bearing different names but same photograph? And now I mean by Exhibit 111.3.

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes. This is identification in the name of Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. So if he had to show a personal ID card together with a refugee ID card, then he wouldn't have been able to do so because these two cards are issued in two different names; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't know what documents he did produce, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When he spoke about the fact that he needed medical assistance and that he used one of these documents for those purposes, did he tell you where he obtained this medical assistance?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I can't recall that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We do not know, Mr. Domazet, where he was living at the time of his arrest. All we know is that he was -- he's been charged with events that happened in, if I can get the pronunciation correct, Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Vlasenica, yes. [Interpretation] Vlasenica, yes. Well, this is why I'm putting this question, in order to comprehend the relevance of questioning of this witness as it concerns Mr. Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, I'm only trying to assist you to get to the real issue. Why don't you simply ask him where was he living at the time of his arrest?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Selsky --

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I was told --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: -- where --

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I was told during the interview the exact name, and I cannot recall that name, but it's in a smaller village on the east side of Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Could I be of assistance and ask you whether that place perhaps is Smederevo?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, that leaves the question: "Who are the issuing authorities of these ID cards?"

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, can it be gleaned from this refugee ID card who are the issuing authorities, whether this is a refugee ID card issued by Republika Srpska or the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I cannot tell from the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: At least two of them are shown as Republika Srpska. I don't know about the third. How is your Cyrillic reading, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The seal of this refugee ID card says "Republika Srpska," and then underneath it says, "CSB," which should be the public security centre in Sarajevo. Then beneath that it says, "Vlasenica," and yet beneath that there is something, "Public security," but I can't see what it is in front, and then it says, "Ministry of the Interior." This means that this is the ID -- refugee ID of Republika Srpska and that Mr. Nikolic identified himself as the refugee in Republika Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you know that Federal Republic of Yugoslavia had special refugee cards, which means that refugees went through a special registration process in Yugoslavia and obtained their refugee ID cards there?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Based on an interview conducted with him, did you find out where he obtained medical treatment? Was it in Federal Republic of Yugoslavia or in Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I didn't specifically ask him that question, I don't believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And when he spoke about very expensive X-rays which he said cost a hundred monthly retirement benefits of his mother, do you know which country he had in mind? Was it Republika Srpska or the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: It wasn't an issue at the time, and I didn't ask him that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What do you mean it wasn't an issue at the time, Mr. Selsky? As regards what?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: From my perspective, it wasn't an issue where he received some medical treatment. It was my understanding -- I was more concerned of the fact that he was using this identification, as an indicted person, not to be apprehended.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: That's what I think, too, Mr. Selsky, but you are here to demonstrate that he used these documents in order to provide free medical care. I don't think this to be the case. I think that he said this on purpose, for reasons known only to him. Do you know whether his mother is alive, the one that had 10 to 15 Deutschemarks in monthly retirement benefits?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: The last time that I spoke with him, it's my understanding that she's still alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. But did she live in Republika Srpska or in Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: She previously lived in Vlasenica. And where exactly she's living at present, I'm not aware of that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you know or did you check whether this claim that at the time one X-ray could have cost 1.500 Deutschemarks, as stated by Mr. Nikolic, is true?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I didn't check, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And did he ever discuss the period in 1992 when he described those medical services?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: It's my recollection that he wasn't referring to the period of 1992 during this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. And just one more question. Do you know when was this indictment issued and when did he find out that there was an indictment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: He dealt with that in the record of interview. You may not want to accept it, but he said it was issued in 1994 or 1995, and he heard about it because somebody else in the town had seen it on television.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not a question of accepting it. I just wanted to verify whether this indeed is that period of time or perhaps a time prior to that. There is a possibility that Dragan Nikolic misstated this on purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, the proceedings bear the number, from memory, 95-2. There was a second indictment filed. It was actually the first one that was issued, I believe. It was certainly the second one filed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. My last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did he ever tell you that he received medical treatment in Visegrad or in Uzice in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: GARRY SELSKY
utterances.text: I explained that to you before. I can't recall. I don't think he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Selsky, a number of people, when they're arrested, have incriminating evidence or evidence which may be incriminating upon them, don't they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And these false identity cards were just such evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: On the face of them, they are incriminating.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And you asked him, in effect, did he have an innocent explanation for having them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indirectly, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And he gave these explanations about needing them for medical attention.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is it still part of the Prosecution case that his possession of these ID cards was incriminating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It's not. Have you accepted his explanation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the face of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. And that is because of the dates that they bear, is it, that they related to sometime more recently? 1998, I think one of them was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It -- in comparison to what he stands before the Tribunal for, it's minuscule, and we really didn't look at it in any other light, and we didn't compare it to any other sources or we didn't investigate his side of the story. We just took it as face.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you want to ask any questions about that, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any re-examination, Mr. Ossogo?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir, for coming along to give evidence. You're now free to leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We'll resume at 2.30. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.05 p.m. 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sir, would you please stand and make the solemn declaration in the form of the document that is being handed to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sit down, please. Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Doctor. Today I will be asking you some questions on behalf of the Defence, and I'd like to ask you one thing: When I ask you my questions, and when my learned friends start to ask you questions, to always make a short break in order to facilitate the work of the interpreters, all the more so as there will no doubt be very many medical terms which are of high relevance and yet are difficult for interpretation. But let us begin with my first question. Could you please give some particulars about you.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: I am Cedomir Vucetic. I am a specialist in orthopaedic surgery and traumatology. I come from Belgrade. I am the head of the orthopaedic team of surgeons at the emergency centre in Belgrade, and the team has five doctors, orthopaedic surgeons. I'm also head of that department at the Institute for Orthopaedic Surgery and Dermatology in Belgrade, and I'm a docent or, if you like, assistant professor at the faculty of medicine in Belgrade. In my clinical work, I engage in the treatment of lower-leg injuries and all the consequences, which means very complicated surgical interventions, the compensation of the replacement and implantation of soft tissues and cartilages, that is, all that is involved in microsurgical interventions. In other words, I have by now acquired considerable experience in this particular area. That, I think, would be enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. You have attached your C.V. to your finding, but I should nevertheless like to ask you to tell us: How many years of service do you have behind you?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: I specialised in orthopaedic surgery and traumatology, and I started doing it since 1988 at the Institute for Orthopaedic Surgery and Traumatology.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And now, although you teach at the faculty of medicine and you are head of all these departments, but are you still an active surgeon? Do you still perform operations?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes, definitely, because that is my primary concern, my principal role. This is my job. And it involves the treatment of the most complex injuries, of the severest injuries, and since I also do microsurgical interventions and amputation of lower legs, of foot, of hands, replantations, and all possible complications, that is, the infection, the emergence of ulcers, defects, or muscular defects, I also apply complex surgical -- microsurgical interventions; that is, I transplant tissues and I apply Ilizarov's method, which is a special method applied in the treatment of complex lower-leg injuries and other injuries. I mention that in particular because I have considerable experience in the treatment of lower-leg injuries and effects of lower-leg injuries.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. The lower leg, because in this case this is very important. As you could see from the material that you were supplied with, we are dealing with a lower-leg injury. Now, on the basis of your finding, I'd like to ask you, but I think you are talking -- you are a speaking a little bit too fast for the interpreters. So will you please, when you give your answers, will you then try to speak a little slower, just a little bit slower. In relation to Mitar Vasiljevic's injuries, you were given the documentation, and you also wrote your finding and your opinion. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: Yes. I can confirm it, yes. Yes. I had it at my disposal. I had x-rays, one dating to 1992, and six x-rays made in 2001. I analysed them, and in view of the problem, the consideration here, I studied them and I submitted my report on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You explain it at the very beginning of your finding under items A and B; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: But did you answer the questions -- rather, did you analyse the finding of Dr. de Grave, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Let's get the report into evidence, shall we? It's going to save an immense amount of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is there any objection to the tender of his report?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. What is your next number? According to me, it's either 35 or 38. There seems to have been some sort of change of numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I may have skipped one. If 35 is free, then I think we could use 35, but I believe 37 was the last marked exhibit on our part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: To be safe, let's make it 38, shall we?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: So that the doctor's report --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: -- which is dated the 22nd of November, will be Exhibit 38, D38. Now, you may take it that we've read it. If you want him to highlight matters or to expand upon them, do so, but we don't want him just to read it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Doctor, I believe you have your report in front of you, and I'd like to ask you, therefore, to ask you some things about the most important parts of this report. There is no need for you to read out this report or to comment on the body of it. I will only invite you to answer my questions, and I possibly will be inviting some comments. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. As for this chapter entitled "Knee," I have no questions in regard of that one, but I will have some questions to ask you about your finding regarding the lower leg. At the very beginning when you say that the x-rays were somewhat deficient, that they had certain shortcomings, could you please explain what it is that is missing and what, according to you, should have been done technically better so that results could be more precise?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: The certain technical shortcomings in the x-rays can be referred to both when we -- it comes to the x-ray performed in 1992. However, the same holds true of the x-rays made in 19 -- 200 -- 2001. Excuse me. The x-rays of 1992 do not show the upper third of the lower leg or the upper end of both the tibia and fibula. It is not visible on these x-rays. One can understand that up to a degree, because very often the length of the lower leg makes it difficult to include its full length in the standard x-ray formats. The x-ray of the knee done in 2001, I observed that it is not indicated anywhere which leg it is, that is, whether it is the left or the right leg. Likewise, the ankle is not marked on one of the x-rays of 2001. These shortcomings, however, are insignificant and basically irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Could you please give us your explanation first with regard to the lower-leg x-ray of the 14th of June, 1992? You had available the copy which I received from the Prosecutor and sent over to you, and you also could see indicated what leg was concerned, because that seemed to be in dispute. Perhaps it would be best if you had before you this x-ray so that you could explain to us what this is all about.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have x-rays which the expert studied, those that I was given by the Prosecution, and I believe they have already been tendered and marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So may I give them to the doctor so that he can have them in front of him? Perhaps we could have it on the ELMO. Will you try to do that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We did try it once before and it didn't work, but it may this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may be of assistance, Prosecution Exhibit 151 and 21.2 are positive images of that, which will show up on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Doctor, so you will have those x-rays in front of you and you will have the positives on the ELMO, which I believe will also be of help. Now, Doctor, will you please explain: Where did you find on this x-ray, say, which leg it is?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I now observe on the monitor that even this mark which I am referring to can be seen on this reproduction which we are using to explain this fact. This mark is in the lower right corner. On the initial x-ray it is marked by a black marker against a black background, so it's poorly visible. And we can see here a circle, and in the circle, the letter "L." Now, part of that "L" is visible here on this light surface, on this light linear surface. I'm pointing at it right now. So that there's no longer a fact in dispute that the initial x-ray was marked indicating that this was the left leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Dr. Vucetic, you are saying that we can see this part, but on the x-ray that you have, can one see this whole circle and letter "L"?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: Yes, one can see it, but one must really have a close look and look at it at a particular angle to light. Light has to fall under a specific angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Very well. Will you then briefly describe to us what you see here on this x-ray? What kind of a fracture is this, according to this fracture [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: This was the initial x-ray made after the injury, and it shows, it represents, a so-called spiral fracture between the lower and the middle third of the tibia. It is characteristic of this fracture that the line of the fracture is S-shaped and that it is drawn out. The effect of such a drawn-out S-shaped fracture is the shortening of the leg at the site of the fracture and a certain dislocation. The leg can be 5 millimetres or more shorter.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Will you explain, Doctor, how does this shortening mean [as interpreted], and what does it mean in practice? How does it happen and what does it mean in practice?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: The shortening is the common phenomenon in most of the fractures of long bones, and that is the lower leg. That is, the mechanism which leads to the shortening should be sought in the fact that the muscles tend to contract, and since the muscles are joined to the bones and the bone is fractured, the length of the muscles is also reduced, and therefore, because of the attachments, the length of the bone as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Doctor, you can go just a little bit more quickly if you wish. It's being taken down very speedily by the typists, and the interpreters are more than keeping up with you, so if you'd like to go just a little bit more quickly, I think it would be easier for us to listen to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Doctor, when you say this, what I'd like to know is if this is perhaps the reason for the extension as the method of treatment, or is it not necessarily the case?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: The extension is a conventional and simple method of treatment of lower-leg fractures, and it was also applied in this case, precisely because of its simplicity and efficiency. Such a fracture can always be treated in different ways. The extension, what was achieved with the extension was to offset the shortening and the dislocation. And after a certain period of time, of course, it provided for the rest of the immobilisation of the site of the fracture so that the bone could begin to heal.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And if I ask you the following: When extension is applied to a fracture like this one, would then such an x-ray following the extension look rather different than the x-ray that you have before you? And if these two x-rays were different, how? In what way would they be different?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: Doubtless the changes are quite noticeable before and after the application of extension. The change can be in the complete correction or perhaps not quite but almost full correction, but improvement is very visible. The effect of the extension is the improvement of the position or full correction. That is the range.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that. That is a medical answer which explains what are the results of the extension. But as far as the x-ray is concerned, would that x-ray be substantially different from the one that was made on the 14th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: Yes. We could say that it would be definitely different in the sense that it would show a correction of the position of fragments.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Would it be possible to establish the beginning and the end of the fracture? Could we establish the dimensions of the fracture, and would that be different on an x-ray after the extension treatment or several weeks after such treatment had begun?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: The changes are definitely visible. There is a general problem here when comparing x-rays after the consolidation of a fracture, namely, nine years after it healed, when we compare these x-rays to the initial ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Doctor, you have used a term "remodelling" or "rebuilding" in your report. Can you tell us what does this term pertain to and what is it about?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: I would like to give several important facts in that regard. One thing is that we use the extension to correct the length and the interrelation of fragments. The other thing is that the healing was completed, which in turn led to forming of new bone tissue at the location where there used to be a fracture line, and in this manner, the line of fracture became either invisible or more difficult to see. The healing itself is supposed to erase the line of fracture. After the bone healed, then there is either an invisible line on fracture or one that can be seen with difficulty, and we also have new bone tissue which can be seen as a thickening not only at the area where there used to be a fracture, and it can perhaps be -- its dimensions could be from several millimetres to perhaps a whole centimetre, and this thickening should be somewhere near the line of fracture. And I would like to add a third fact which has been mentioned by Mr. Domazet and that is the rebuilding process or remodelling process which typically takes place and lasts years after the healing of the fracture. The essence of this process amounts to reabsorption of the bone and reforming of the bone tissue simultaneously, which leads to a change in architecture or in the form of a bone and its structure in the area where there used to be a fracture which had healed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, there's another word there used in his report very shortly after the word "remodelation" in which I'd be grateful for some assistance on --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: "Rebuilding."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: -- "morphology." You see on the last page? I've got the English version. Perhaps I'll just ask the doctor directly. What do you mean by "morphology," Doctor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the basic sense, that is the appearance of the fracture that has healed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Doctor, before we proceed any further and speak about changes that can come with time, I would like to go back to the x-ray that was made on the 14th of June, 1992 and ask you the following: In your report, you said something that you've also repeated here, and you said that there was a fracture of tibia and, namely, a spiral fracture. In your report, you said that part of the fibula visible on this x-ray is without any x-ray indication of a fracture, and you said that it is not typical for such fracture not to be visible in two different x-rays; however, this is possible or it's possible that there should be a small fracture. So could you please clarify this? It is possible that there could be a crack. So could you please explain this further to us?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: Strictly medically speaking, such type of fractures are possible, and they're usually called fissures or cracks. What is typical for them is that there is no movement at the spot where there is a fissure. And also, there is a barely visible or even invisible line of fracture. But I should say that the fracture of fibula that can be observed here and that is seen as something that had healed - this can be seen on the x-rays made in 2001 - can be directly linked to the fact that Mr. Mitar Vasiljevic had an injury, a fracture of the same leg in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Are you trying to tell us, Doctor, that on an x-ray from 1992, in a spot where in current x-rays from 2001 there can be seen a trace of fibula fracture, is not something that can be seen from the x-ray from 1992?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: The fracture is not visible. The fracture is not visible on the x-ray from 1991, although theoretically we cannot exclude it. However, it is not visible on the x-rays.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Sir, you just said in your previous answer "1991." That was probably a slip of tongue. Did you, in fact, mean 1992?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Would it be possible, Doctor, that in 1992 there was either a fracture or a fissure of fibula, but in an area that cannot be seen on an x-ray which is in front of you, meaning on the upper part of the leg, and that is not shown on the x-ray? Since this injury is indisputable, would it be possible to have that kind of a fracture of fibula?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: Well, that is quite possible. That is a realistic possibility, in view of the spot where there was a fracture. However, the x-rays made in 2001, showing the upper part of fibula, do not have any signs of a fracture which used to be there and perhaps healed. So I would like to point to another valuable fact, which is that the patient had an injury in 1993, namely, a fracture of the lower leg, and I would be more inclined to link this injury of fibula to the injury from 1993. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So let us just be completely specific. When you mention injury from 1993, do you mean the injury that can be seen on x-rays from 2001, indicating that there was an injury of fibula?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Now, would it be possible, since you have said that theoretically it is possible that there was a fracture of fibula in the upper part, when we are talking about the injury of tibia, so would that be possible that that fracture or fissure has healed in the meantime but due to the passage of time - and we are talking about nine years - it is now invisible in the x-rays made in 2001? Would there be a possibility for this explanation to be realistic?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. This very fact that nine years have passed can be a significant influence on the visibility of such a fracture, especially if it's a fracture that represents a minor dislocation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Could you also explain to us what changes can take place during nine years and what can acquire a different appearance in current x-rays as compared to the x-rays of the same leg from 1991?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: Well, these changes can be caused by a number of factors. One group of factors have to do with the fact that nine years have passed, and that is a significant period of time for anyone. Changes occur naturally. There are some degenerative changes that take place and also those in the structure of bone. There could be osteoporosis, which is to say there can be a change in the amount of calcium, and this is a substance that can be clearly seen in x-rays. The second group of factors has to do with the process of remodelling. This process leads to changes in the bone that are such that the morphology or the form of the bone is adjusted to the functional requirements, or, simply speaking, certain curves or rough spots can be corrected after a number of years have passed. The process of remodelation is very intense in a young person, so that the adolescents, their fractures become invisible after several years due to the very process of remodelation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Dr. Vucetic, you have examined several x-rays of the same leg made in 2001, and based on what you wrote in your report, you also described this fracture as a spiral one. Am I right? And could you comment on these x-rays from 2001, and if there is -- and tell us whether there is any difference when we compare these x-rays to the ones made in 1992. And please specify what kind of differences can be observed.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: This healed fracture of the lower leg seen on x-rays from 2001 can definitely be described as a spiral fracture. The outline of the fracture is clear, and it corresponds, in view of its shape and location on the tibia, to the x-ray from 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Dr. Vucetic, in view of this, do you believe -- do you believe that these x-rays, meaning those from 2001 and 1992, are the x-rays of the same leg of the same patient? Are the signs of fracture compatible, in view of the changes described by you?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think this is something questionable at all. Looking at the fracture line seen in the X-rays from 2001 as well is something that we can use to support this view. We can also compare this with the form and structure of this bone and other bones that are seen on the x-rays.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Before we proceed any further with this, I would like to ask you the following as regards your opinion of these x-rays: The possibility of this spiral fracture is something that I would like to investigate. How does this kind of fracture come about, and how does it differ from other types of fractures which are also common?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: The spiral fracture occurs when there is a twisting. One part of the lower leg is -- either the lower part or upper part of it has to be fixed, and there also has to be some twisting when the fracture occurs, the fracture that has this type of line. When there are direct or indirect blows in the lower leg, then the fractures that we call perpendicular fractures usually occur, or transversal fractures, although fractures can involve the ones where there are a number of fragments, and we can also have a fracture with an oblique line.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Dr. Vucetic, would it be possible for the fracture that can be seen on these X-rays and in the absence of any incompatibilities, as you have stated, to occur when there is a fall as described by Mr. Vasiljevic, which is to say a fall from a horse on the side when the horse also falls down on the victim? Would this kind of fracture be compatible with the described situation? Would it be common in that situation or would it be something not typical? Could you give us opinion regarding that, please?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: This type of injury would be possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, I'm afraid the doctor has been led into the use of that word "possible" by your question. You changed your question towards the end of it, but it has to be something which is reasonably possible to start with. It is a significant difference. But then you asked him, was it compatible, was it typical. I think those were the two words you used, was it "compatible" and "not typical." May I suggest you ask him again and use the word -- if you again use the word "possibility," that you add the word "reasonable" to it, because it has to be a reasonable possibility for there to be a failure to prove something beyond reasonable doubt.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Dr. Vucetic, you heard the Honourable Judge. So is it reasonably possible to have this type of an injury, and how likely is it under these circumstances?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: I understood the Judge's comments and your question as well. I think that it is very probable that that is how the spiral fracture occurred, and I base this on the fact that the fracture occurred when Mitar was moving. And then as he was moving and fell, it is very likely that there could have been some kind of a rotational movement which led to this twisting, which in turn led to this type of injury. If we also knew that the foot was in fact fixed in the stirrups, then that would even further confirm that there was some twisting there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: There weren't any stirrups, as I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That is what I was going to ask. So we did not have a stirrup in this case so the leg was not fixed. If I understand you, if there is a stirrup, then there is a greater possibility to have twisting. However, could there be twisting regardless of whether the horse fell to that side as well over that leg? And do you think that this is relevant in view -- this would be relevant even if the fracture took place before the horse fell on him?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: Well, we have to stick to the presumption that something fixed, most probably the foot, and I believe that that was the horse, or his leg was stuck somehow. But his body, that was moving together with the horse, continued this movement, this rotational movement, and this is the mechanism that led to a spiral fracture.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Doctor, when you say that the foot was fixed, would that be in the case when that foot touches the surface onto which the body is falling, and in that case the leg can rotate, and leading, conducing, to such a fracture?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: Well, one can make such an assumption, yes, but it is hard to say how reasonable that assumption is. But such a mechanism is definitely possible. It depends on the speed of the movement, the bone structure, and so on and so forth. But any kind of resistance when the body is rotating - that is, that the lower leg, with the foot, follows the rotation of the body -- can, under certain conditions, can lead to such a spiral fracture.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you speak about movement, that the body is in motion, did you also remember that the fall takes place while the horse is still moving and that it is therefore shifting the rider? That is, did you also take note of the form of -- of the type of movement involved?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: Well, all this plays a role, but it is really difficult to make any conclusions with any certainty as to what happened in reality. I mean, it cannot go beyond speculation. However, it is quite a realistic assumption that we can make, that is, that the injured person and the horse were in contact at the moment when the fracture took place. It is quite realistic to say that there was a contact between the injured person and the horse and that that is the reason for the fracture of this type.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And as regards the ground onto which the person is falling, does it play a role? Does it determine anything? If we are dealing with a completely flat surface, would there be any difference if this surface were not completely flat?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: Basically, regardless of the surface onto which one is falling, the fact that the injured person fell from a certain height, at a certain speed of movement, must have produced a fracture.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you mean that such a fracture could occur both on a completely flat surface and on a rough surface?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Would such a fracture be possible if a vehicle hit a pedestrian? That is, in the case of a traffic accident, when a vehicle hits a pedestrian, is such a fracture possible, too, or isn't it?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: One could not exclude that possibility, but it is a fact that it is quite atypical. It is characteristic that when fractures are due to a vehicle hitting the lower leg, that the bone is split into several fragments, that is, that it is a multi-fracture, or these are usually oblique or transversal fractures. Spiral fractures are not characteristic fractures in such cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Would this cause --

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: No. A spiral fracture does not occur in such cases. One can take it as a fact. The spiral fracture is not due when a vehicle strikes, hits, the lower leg of a person.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Now, Doctor, I'd like to ask you something else, and that is the part on which you also commented in your report, even though in your introduction you did not say that you also had this kind of documentation. But nevertheless, I'd like to ask you if you also had -- when you were writing your report, did you have the findings of Dr. Yvan de Grave before you?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I had Dr. Yvan de Grave's report at my disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You addressed this in the part of your report headed "Discussion," in which you make a comparison between those x-rays and give your reasons as to what can be the cause for the discrepancies between the x-rays. So could you please explain a little this? Could you please explain what you meant by this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, he's really done that, has he not? He's explained about the healing process, and that's why the one from 1992 is shorter than the one in 2001. I don't know what more he can do except repeat what he's written. If you want him to explain a particular part of it, by all means go to it, but he's made it very clear his explanation for the fact that the 1992 x-ray and the one that is taken in 2001, the difference in the length can be disregarded because of the healing process. At some stage we're going to have to deal with the fact that the one in 2001 is longer than the one in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Perhaps it is best to directly address the results which are represented here by Dr. Yvan de Grave. You saw some of the x-rays and some of the charts that he drew regarding the injury and comparing the fractures, or rather, the x-rays of 1992 and 2001. Could you please tell us if that was possible, and was that done in a manner which you would consider medically reliable?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: This is a very important question, and it needs to be cleared up. With all the sensitiveness involved in comparing x-rays taken at a nine-year interval, one must bear in mind that considerable methodological mistakes were committed in the definition of the fracture line, or rather, fracture plane. On this occasion, I should like to point at these errors. As we can see on the monitor, the first x-ray, the initial x-ray, has marked certain lines, which would be the lines of fracture, or rather, the plane of the fracture. Now, I would like to start my explanation with a fact that a spiral fracture looks like a drawn-out letter "S". In some of its segments, this line has a different angle, a different inclination. And we can see here that the median part of this fracture line was used to define the plane of the fracture or, rather, the inclination, and that the final point of the line of the fracture in the upper part of the lower leg and the lower part of the lower leg were disregarded. Now, the x-rays of 2001, we have a poorly visible fracture line, and the callus or, rather, the new bone tissue, it fills in not only the fracture line and appears not only at the place of the fracture but it starts quite far away from the fracture itself, and that is how a bone heals. And this radiographic sign that we are dealing with, that there is new bone on the tibia, that there is new osseous tissue on the tibia is indicated as the upper point, the upper end of the fracture line, hence this methodological error in determining the fracture line and subsequent erroneous conclusion that these are two different fractures.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Doctor, when you say an error in determining the line in this conclusion, what is it that you mean and whom do you mean? Whose error do you think it is?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: The error which appears or the explanation which is provided in the report of the expert de Grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Could we -- could you possibly indicate it, point at the drawing that he did, and could you use it to explain what you've just told us but unfortunately could not show?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That is Exhibit P21.3, the schematic one. Is that the one you want?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You see, my problem, and we might as well face up to it, I want an explanation. There may well be one. I'm not so concerned about the error that could well have been made in the plane of the fracture. What I'm concerned about are the measurements which Dr. de Grave took above the dome of the heel as to where the fracture began and where it ended. We are not talking about the length of the fracture. We're talking about the difference in the height above the dome Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. of the heel. And the one in 1992 was shorter than the one in 2001. Now, the doctor has explained very well, if I may say so, that one would expect a fracture to become shorter when you look at it in x-rays taken many years after the event because of the healing process, but that's not this case. It appears to be longer. And it may be that Dr. de Grave made an error in where the fracture lines began and ended, but that's where I think, if I may say so, you should direct your questions, because that is the issue in the case. There's also an issue which this doctor has not referred to in his report and that was the shape of the heel, the calcaneum, I think you call it, which Dr. de Grave placed some emphasis on. Now, those are the two issues that Dr. de Grave pointed, and I think this doctor has to deal with them, and he doesn't, if I may say so, in his report. So that's what we're really after. And we really want some assistance, because it's a very fascinating and a difficult problem.
