I should add there's no way we're going to finish this by 4.00, but at some stage, I would like you to take it, because I'm sure Mr. Groome is going to take him to it as well, and I've gone around the report in great detail and it's been of assistance, but at some stage we have to face up to these real issues in the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. And I never thought that this problem of the heel and what Witness de Grave explained, to leave it out, and that is included in my questions and we shall eventually get there. Whether it will be today, I doubt that. But I nevertheless go by the report provided by the doctor rather than the inconsistency.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Could you please place it on the ELMO and point at it?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: Yes. I understood your question and the question posed by the President of the Chamber. But perhaps I could start from here. Yes. I wanted this x-ray somewhere here. It is pretty arbitrary really, that is, we can pick out any point here because there are a quite a number of lines here. Now, on this diagram, I cannot really show it. I can do it on an x-ray. There are several lines in the structure of the bone which may be considered as the trace, as the remnant of the fracture line in these x-rays. It is fact that Dr. de Grave took the lowest point as the end point of the fracture line, and that again is a matter under question. I mean, one can wonder really whether that is indeed so. It is a matter for personal view, for a personal opinion. That was his personal impression. When looking at this fracture line, I couldn't really fully agree that that is indeed the fracture line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just one moment, Doctor. Seeing that we're going to have to stand this over at some stage, I wonder, Mr. Domazet, if you could ask the doctor to draw a similar diagram to 21.3 and have him mark where he says the fractures began and finished so that we can get his schematic representation of the -- where each fracture began and finished. Now, it may be difficult to do, I don't know, but it is this which Dr. de Grave relies upon, and if this witness can demonstrate that there is a reasonable possibility that Dr. de Grave was wrong, well, then that's a fundamental point in your client's case, and it will assist us, I think, if we have a similar diagram by him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I presume when he resumes his testimony that he should draw this sketch by then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, I'm only asking. I'm not ordering. It may be difficult for him to do, I don't know. But if he'd like to take the x-rays to do it, we would be very grateful for his assistance. At some stage, of course, the Prosecution will probably want to show those X-rays and his diagram to their specialist.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I believe that Dr. Vucetic understands what he's asked to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And of course, Doctor, if you can, because we shall have to adjourn today and your testimony will be resumed after some time, after a rather long break, so do you think you would be able to draw a similar sketch so that it will be easier for you and everybody to make comparisons?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VUCETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Very well, I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And one final point that I have in my mind: We've had some rather vague evidence about the injury which your client says he had in 1993, and I would like to know whether there's anything on the 2001 x-rays which demonstrates that there was another injury, that is, two injuries in roughly the same spot. At one stage, we were told that it was some centimetres above or below the other fracture - I'm not sure when it was - but then we've had different descriptions. But I want to know if there's anything on the more recent x-rays which shows another fracture there, which may in itself explain the length, the additional length of the fracture shown on the 2001 x-ray. But there are a lot of problems arising out of this, and I am hoping that your doctor will be able to give us some assistance on it. Well, now, I don't know whether you've got some other questions to ask him now. There are a few housekeeping matters we've got to deal with before we finish this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, Doctor, I'm very sorry we can't finish with you. We're having a lot of trouble getting the evidence finished in this case. I can assure you it is not for want of trying by the Trial Chamber. In fact, you may ask your counsel here to show you some of the scars he probably bears from the attempts we've made from trying to get the witnesses to finish their evidence. We will have to resume again with you on the -- in early January. I'm sure Mr. Domazet can sort out with you which will be the most convenient time for you. So we'll let you go now. We will see you back here, I'm afraid, next year.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, you can go now, Doctor, whilst we deal with the few remaining things that we have to before we go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, may I ask you, first of all, when you read those statutory provisions, you were clearly not reading from this opinion that you've now provided us with because they're not quoted in there. I think you said you had these provisions in Serbo-Croatian - I'm sorry. We must be more politically correct - the B/C/S name, which we've checked our library edition. It's not as modern as yours. We do have an English translation of an earlier version, but are you able to provide us with the statutory provisions in B/C/S and we can get them translated? That's about the recording.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I've got it ready. Doctor, perhaps you could take with you these x-rays. You might need them, and we will not be needing them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We will need them back.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. These are copies of the x-rays that I was -- that the Prosecution disclosed to us. Your Honour, I have here a photocopy of that page of the Official Gazette which carried the Criminal Proceedings Act of 2000, if that is what you meant, in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have it here in some ten copies, and I can leave it with the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I have in mind that we have not yet admitted the tapes and the transcripts. The evidence of the witness is sufficient to get it in. Whether we accept her evidence in the end is a different matter and what we make of the tapes is a different matter, but the actual evidence of the witness that it was an accurate transcription of what was said would be a sufficient basis for getting the tapes into evidence. So in those circumstances, we will admit those tapes. What is your next number, Mr. Groome? You jump all over the place, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't have the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The last one that we have -- the highest number of yours that we have is 165.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: They were already numbered. If we can just take a look at -- if you can just give me a minute to get the exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You mean the tapes and the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes. We're all pre-numbered. I think it was 109, Your Honour, but I'm a little reluctant to -- I see the court -- 109.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. It's 109.4A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And 4B.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And 4B, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And just if I might add to that, that's the copy of the original tape, audio cassette. 109 one was the CD itself of the enhanced version.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 109 is the CD.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And the transcripts?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I have --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, 109.1 was the B/C/S transcript and 109.2 was the transcript in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Mr. Domazet, as I have explained, the witness's evidence was sufficient to make them admissible. The weight to be given to them is a matter which we'll have to resolve later. Is there anything you want to add about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand, Your Honour. However, I'd like to seize this opportunity to see if I can do something with these cassettes, that is, to subject them to expertise. Of the two cassettes that I was given, one has about 20 minutes and the other one only 5 minutes are used up, and Mr. Groome told me that it was twice an-hour-length recordings. So perhaps I wasn't given the right cassettes, or perhaps not the fully recorded cassettes, or perhaps there is an error there, and I'd like to avoid any future problems with that. So perhaps I'll be able to resolve it with Mr. Groome when we adjourn, or perhaps there is an explanation why this difference in the length of the recordings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: There's also this point, Mr. Domazet, which you might like to resolve with Mr. Groome. If you want to have this checked to see whether there are stoppages on it, whether it's been stopped at any time or whether there's been any interference with it, you would have to have, would you not, the original tape? Because copying it masks this sort of problem, from my perhaps peripheral experience of these sorts of cases. I gather you should have the original tape. Is that available, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sure, if Mr. Domazet identifies the expert he wishes to examine, we'll make arrangements to have that securely sent to that person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Can I leave it to you to deal with between you?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, in the meantime, those tapes and transcripts will be Exhibits 109, 109.1, 109.2, 109.4A, 109.4B, each of them with a "P" for Prosecution in front of them. But I think that must be so, Mr. Groome. The original is necessary, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The Prosecution has no objection to providing that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Domazet, you had undertaken during the break to find out from the nearest meteorological records what dusk or what sunset would have been in Visegrad at the relevant time, and you will look after that, will you, over the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I will do that, and as soon as I get it, I will send it, regardless of the recess. I will send it for the Judges and for the Prosecution, even though in the Muslim calendar for 2002, which the - for 1992, excuse me - which the Prosecution had tendered, I believe there is also the calendar for sunrise and sunset in 1992, except that one cannot see which part of Bosnia-Herzegovina is involved. But I would not say that the differences would be all that big.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You have introduced a new terror. I didn't realise we were working on the Muslim calendar, what with the Serb calendar being different as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No. [Interpretation] That is the calendar of Muslim Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. holidays, the calendar for 1992, but with Muslim red-letter days, and I was given it by the Prosecution. And for every one of these days, it shows the sunrise, the sunset, and the same for the moon. So it's not a Muslim -- it's not following Muslim recording, but just the calendar with Muslim holidays, and also just as I have given the Prosecution a calendar with Orthodox holidays.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Bosnia-Herzegovina is a very large area, and this is on one side of it. I think that we would appreciate a more exact indication of when sunset was so that we can attempt to work out when dusk was. Now, the final thing that I say will only be repetition, but I want to repeat it so that you go from here with it ringing in your ears. You will have to spend time during your vacation preparing your final addresses. We are under a very, very tight schedule for next year. And what I suggest is that you deal with the evidence which comes next year orally during the course of your final submissions, and you prepare your written submissions on the basis of the evidence as it presently stands. We will be commencing on Wednesday, the 9th of January, to enable Mr. Domazet and his team to spend the Serbian Christmas, Orthodox Christmas, with their families, but that comes at a price, I'm afraid, and that is working during the vacation. We have to finish the whole hearing - and I'm talking now about courts administration - to enable another trial to start on the 21st. Now, that is fairly immovable, as I understand it. There was a Pre-Trial Conference yesterday, and the Pre-Trial Judge apparently said that, without any doubt, it would start. Now, one of the Judges in this particular Trial Chamber is sitting on that case, so it has to be -- we have to finish by that time. That gives us eight sitting days. Now, with all of the evidence we have to go, as I understand it, there are a number of specialists whose reports, of course, would go in as their evidence in chief, with a brief expansion on those parts which are important, and cross-examination. But you'll see that we are very, very pressed for time. I would like to say that we will hear the final addresses on the Thursday and the Friday of the week before the 21st, so that would be the 17th and the 18th, I think, of January. So you'll see where we are next year. Well, with that, may I wish you all a happy Orthodox and non-Orthodox Christmas, and we'll see you in the new year.
